original_question: What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.11 in Section 6.3 (“Quantum integrability for polynomial in momenta integrals”): “What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?”
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target almost verbatim. It has the right object (the metric g), the right classical system (the geodesic flow), the right class of integrals (polynomial in momenta), and the right goal (quantisability of every such integral). It also stays with Problem 6.11 rather than drifting to the broader quantisation question of Section 6.1 or the more special Lie-group/argument-shift problem 6.12.
missing_details: The paper’s setting is a Riemannian manifold (M, g), not an unspecified metric space or abstract metric object.

The classical system should be stated explicitly: the geodesic flow is the Hamiltonian flow on T^*M of H(x,p) = (1/2) g^{ij}(x) p_i p_j, i.e. the case U = 0 of the natural Hamiltonian H = K + U in equation (1).
A “polynomial integral” means a first integral F(x,p) satisfying {H, F} = 0 that is polynomial in the momenta p_i, with coefficients depending on x.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the property is required for every polynomial first integral F of the geodesic flow, not merely for the existence of some quantisable integral.
No homogeneity assumption and no degree restriction are imposed in Problem 6.11; the question ranges over polynomial integrals of arbitrary degree.

“Quantisable” must be defined: there must exist a differential operator F-hat on functions on M that commutes with the quantum Hamiltonian H-hat = Delta_g (the Beltrami-Laplace operator in the geodesic case) and whose symbol is F.
The paper notes that self-adjointness of F-hat is optional (“Sometimes one requires ...”); it is not part of Problem 6.11 itself.
The ambient setting is the usual real cotangent-bundle Hamiltonian picture; no nilpotency condition, characteristic-p variant, or ‘for all sufficiently large m’ clause appears here.
The paper imposes no dimension restriction in Problem 6.11; that absence should be left explicit rather than silently specialized.
refined_question: Let (M, g) be a Riemannian manifold, let H(x,p) = (1/2) g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j be the geodesic Hamiltonian on T^*M with its canonical symplectic structure, and let H-hat = Delta_g be the corresponding Beltrami-Laplace operator on functions on M. Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on g under which every first integral F(x,p) of H that is polynomial in the momenta p_i admits a differential operator F-hat on M such that [H-hat, F-hat] = 0 and the symbol of F-hat is F.
justification: The draft is already essentially the exact wording of Problem 6.11, so the main task is not to broaden it but to make it stand alone by unpacking the paper’s local notation and definitions. Section 6.3 supplies the quantum side: H-hat = Delta + U, the commutator condition for a quantum integral, and the definition of “quantisable.” Section 2.1 supplies the classical Hamiltonian H = (1/2)g^{ij}p_i p_j + U, explains that the geodesic-flow case is U = 0, and defines what “polynomial in momenta” means. That is the narrowest paper-faithful refinement of your draft.
